content:
Gurugram's property market is crowded in a very specific way. Several new projects often launch in the same stretch at the same time, whether along Dwarka Expressway, Golf Course Extension Road or Sohna Road, and they all target the same buyers with similar ads. A buyer searching for a 3 BHK in New Gurgaon can see ten brochures in a week. In that situation, the job of digital marketing is not simply to "generate leads". It is to find genuine buyers, get them to a site visit, and keep the sales team from wasting time on the rest.

TopWebExpert runs real estate digital marketing in Gurugram from our office on Sohna Road in Sector 49, a short drive from many of the new launches in the area. This page explains how we plan campaigns around a project's stage, what the compliance requirements are, and what a developer or channel partner should expect from us.

Who we work with, and how the work differs

Developers usually need the full picture: a project website or landing pages, search and social campaigns, and lead routing to an in-house sales team and to channel partners. Channel partners handling mandates for several projects need fast, low-cost landing pages per project and tight lead tracking, because their margin depends on it. Independent brokers dealing in resale and rentals in areas like Sushant Lok, DLF Phases or Sector 56 need a different approach: local search visibility, a Google Business Profile and listing-portal management, rather than big ad budgets.

Compliance comes first

Property advertising in Haryana is regulated, and ads that break the rules put the project and the advertiser at risk. Before any campaign goes live we check:

  • The project is registered with HARERA (Gurugram), and its registration number is shown on every ad, landing page and brochure, along with the authority's website where required.
  • Channel partners and brokers advertising the project hold their own RERA agent registration and display it.
  • Claims such as possession dates, amenities, distances and approvals match what is registered and what the developer can document.
  • Price mentions are clear about what is and isn't included, so they do not mislead.
  • Pre-launch "EOI" campaigns for projects that are not yet registered are handled with care. We do not run ads that sell or take bookings for an unregistered project.

We also follow Google's and Meta's own advertising policies, which reject ads for vague or misleading property claims.

Campaigns by project stage

Pre-launch and launch

This is when demand is highest and competition is fiercest. We build a fast-loading landing page with floor plans, the location map, price band and RERA details, then run Google Search campaigns on project and location searches, plus Meta campaigns with lead forms to reach buyers who aren't searching yet. Budgets usually peak here, and lead volume is watched daily.

Sustenance

After launch interest fades, inventory still needs to move. We shift towards remarketing to past site visitors, construction update videos, specific unit types that are left, and search campaigns on narrower terms. Cost per lead often rises, so lead quality becomes the main focus.

Ready to move in

For completed or near-complete projects, the selling point is certainty. We use walkthrough videos, photos of the actual site, possession details and nearby infrastructure. Search terms like "ready to move flats" plus a sector or road perform well at this stage.

Where the enquiries come from

  • Google Search ads
  • Meta lead forms
  • Instagram Reels
  • YouTube walkthroughs
  • Landing page forms
  • Click-to-WhatsApp ads
  • Google Business Profile
  • Property portals

We don't use every channel for every project. A luxury project on Golf Course Road and an affordable housing project in Sohna need very different mixes, and we plan the split with you based on buyer profile and budget.

The follow-up problem

In our experience, the biggest leak in property marketing is not the ads. It is what happens after the form is submitted. Meta lead forms in particular bring many people who tapped "submit" without much thought, and if a sales executive calls them the next day, the interest has gone.

  1. Every lead is pushed instantly into your CRM (or a shared sheet if you don't have one yet), tagged with the source, campaign and project.
  2. An automatic WhatsApp or SMS goes out within minutes with the brochure and a site visit booking link.
  3. The lead is assigned to a salesperson, who is expected to call quickly. We track how fast that happens.
  4. Sales marks each lead as not reachable, not interested, budget mismatch, visit booked, visit done or booked unit.
  5. We use those statuses to cut campaigns and audiences that bring poor leads, even if their cost per lead looks cheap.

This requires honest feedback from your sales team. Without it, we can only optimise for form fills, which is not the same as buyers.

What you receive each month

  • Campaign management on the agreed platforms, with daily budget checks during launch periods.
  • New ad creatives and copy as inventory, offers or construction stages change.
  • Landing page updates, including price, payment plan and availability changes.
  • A report showing leads, cost per lead, cost per site visit and, where your CRM allows, cost per booking, broken down by channel.
  • A review call with recommendations for the next month.

What we need from you: approved creatives or brand guidelines, RERA details, floor plans, price sheets, a named person who can approve ads quickly, and access to lead statuses in your CRM.

When we are not the right fit

We are probably not right for you if you want campaigns for a project without RERA registration, if you want to run ads with a price or possession date the developer hasn't confirmed, or if your team cannot follow up leads within the same day. We are also not a listing portal. We don't sell pre-verified buyer data, and we'd advise you to be careful with anyone who does.

FAQ

Why are my Facebook property leads so poor?

Usually the form is too easy to submit, the audience is too broad, or the follow-up is slow. Adding a qualifying question (budget or unit type), switching to a higher-intent form type and calling within minutes normally improves quality. We check which of these is the problem in your account.

Should a channel partner run ads on a developer's project name?

Many do, but check your mandate agreement first. Some developers restrict bidding on the project name or require approved creatives. We follow whatever your agreement allows.

How long before we see site visits?

Search campaigns can start producing enquiries within days of going live. Site visits depend on your follow-up and the project's appeal, and the first few weeks are used to learn which channels and audiences bring serious buyers.

How is the budget decided?

It depends on the project's price segment, how many competing launches are nearby, the number of units to sell and the timeline. Ad spend is separate from our management fee. We give a fixed quote for our work after a free consultation.

Do you handle projects outside Gurugram?

Yes. Our focus, though, is Gurugram and its surrounding markets, including Sohna, Manesar and Dwarka Expressway, because being close by helps us understand the micro-markets buyers compare.

If you are planning a launch or want to fix an existing campaign, meet us at our office in Spaze I-Tech Park on Sohna Road, Sector 49, or call +91 9050126213. Book a free consultation and bring your current lead reports; we will tell you where the leaks are.
